meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.title: Everolimus Aging Study (EVERLAST): Clinical Evaluation of mTORC1 Inhibition for Geroprotection

evidence.label: Registered trial, no results yet
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Phase 2 trial (NCT05835999, EVERLAST) testing this Atlas's open dosing hypothesis directly: whether daily low-dose (0.5 mg/day) or weekly (5 mg/week) everolimus for 24 weeks can improve physiological and molecular hallmarks of aging in insulin-resistant or prediabetic adults aged 55-80, without the metabolic penalty seen with continuous higher-dose rapalog use. Double-blind and placebo-controlled with four arms (everolimus daily, everolimus weekly, and a matching placebo for each), n=106, plus a separate untreated 18-35 cohort for comparison. Primary endpoint is peripheral insulin sensitivity by dual-tracer OGTT; mTORC1 and mTORC2 signalling are secondary endpoints in muscle and blood cells. STATUS: the registry records the trial as COMPLETED, with primary completion 2026-06-30 and completion 2026-07-22. No results are posted yet, so there is nothing to read into the outcome either way.
data.abstract_excerpt: The objective of this project is to determine if mTORC1 inhibition by 24 weeks of daily (0.5 mg/day) or weekly (5 mg/week) everolimus can safely improve physiological and molecular hallmarks of aging in humans. Participants who are 55-80 years old and insulin resistant or prediabetic will be randomized to treatment and can expect to be on study for up to approximately 38 weeks; participants aged 18-35 will not receive the intervention and can expect to be on study up to approximately 8 weeks.
